evidence: Affected mode accepts only full Git commit identities, derives the complete base-to-head path set with no caller path-subset option, and rejects empty, absolute, drive-qualified, backslash, traversal, whitespace, and control-character paths.

The schema-1.1 selection record freezes exact changed paths, requested profiles, selected and deferred command IDs, matched rules, rationale codes and text, fallback, deferred owner W1-exit, inactive optionals, and the canonical inventory hash. Selection report SHA-256: 8f3163c97f694d4337f06f04eed09042f76a0a115ec3d76a28d8cfa18ee7f0c2.

Any unknown path in a mixed set and every safety-sensitive verification, evidence-control, security, migration, dependency, or threshold surface selects the complete requested active profile inventory; a mapped command outside the requested profiles fails closed.

The final exact candidate has no diff in verification-profiles.json or verification/baselines. Selector tests also deep-compare the in-memory command/profile graph before and after selection, including command arguments and optional activation behavior.
Every new controlled submission freezes non-empty privacy-safe command IDs that must resolve exactly to keys in verification-profiles.json.

Each prospective completed review stores only task/amendment/attempt IDs, submitted/reviewed timestamps and nonnegative duration, outcome, severity/blocking/total counts, canonical command IDs, and prior/replayed/closed remediation linkage; semantic validation recomputes the event exactly.

Strict schemas and recursive canary tests reject or omit reviewer identity, commit/hash/branch, evidence and user-data paths, rationale/root cause, notes, finding bodies, raw commands/arguments/output, prompts, sources, research data, secrets, and chain-of-thought from telemetry.

review-telemetry projects only stored events in deterministic task/round order, emits no generated timestamp, excludes pending submissions, and produced [] for the two historical T01 rounds rather than inventing timing data.

Ordinary full-profile mode retains its schema-1.0 behavior. Affected mode is explicit and cannot be combined with Wave-exit mode; W1 Wave exit uses the fixed approved profile union and cannot be narrowed with --profile.

The W1 exit selection proof resolves 33 active canonical commands with no deferred IDs while leaving inactive optional ai, graph, and e2e-local commands truthful and server/cloud release-gated. Actual complete product/deployment execution remains owned by W1 exit and was not replaced by this task-level foundation run.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: T02 changes shared verification selection, evidence submission, review telemetry, their strict schema, and associated governance documentation. The credible risks are caller-controlled path laundering, incomplete or nondeterministic command partitions, unsafe fallback weakening, mutation of canonical profiles or thresholds, arbitrary command IDs, privacy leakage through reused evidence/review objects, fabricated historical durations, telemetry tamper, and replacement of the complete Wave-exit matrix by a task subset. Exact Git-derived selector tests, recursive privacy canaries, schema/semantic tamper tests, the full active foundation profile, live empty historical telemetry projection, immutable-profile diff, and governed W1-exit resolution cover those risks. The first affected run retained a build-manifest failure caused by three B00 schemas missing from packaging/build-inputs.json; the strict-descendant correction inventories only those schemas, and the complete final-candidate run passes.
